note.headline: Risk snaps back hard as mega-cap tech and small caps rally together
note.standfirst: The S&P 500 rose +4.73% and the Russell 2000 gained +3.40% in a broad, high-breadth rally that reversed last week's damage. VIX collapsed -25.83% to 26.62 but still sits above its long-run range, so positioning should treat this as relief, not an all-clear.
takeaways: Breadth was overwhelming, with 20 advancers against 5 decliners and a 4.0 ratio, confirming this was an index-wide bid, not a single-stock event.
The curve bear steepened even as risk rallied: yields fell across the board but the long end fell less, with 30-year down only 9bp against 15bp at the 5-year.
Credit confirmed the equity move, with high yield and EM sovereign spreads both richer and HYG and EMB among the session's extreme readings.
The dollar firmed to a fresh high even as gold and silver rose, an unusual combination that argues for a short-covering or repositioning flow rather than a clean risk-on signal.
note.desk_view:
This session confirms that the prior leg down was positioning-driven, not fundamental. The snapback in NVDA (+31.48%), ORCL (+12.34%) and TSLA (+11.46%) alongside a Russell 2000 gain of +3.40% says both ends of the risk curve got bought at once, which only happens when forced sellers are done and dealers are short gamma. The MOVE index fell -5.08% and VVIX fell -14.97%, both pointing to a vol-selling flow that amplified the rally mechanically as much as any new information did.

The level that decides whether this holds is the 10-year breakeven, now at 2.13 and printing session lows alongside the 5-year breakeven at 2.15. Falling breakevens into a bear-steepening curve with real yields also lower is the one piece of the picture that does not fit a clean growth-optimism story. If breakevens keep sliding while nominal yields hold, that is a disinflation read the equity rally is not pricing. If they stabilize, today's move looks more like pure repositioning around an oversold tape. Watch that spread before trusting the follow-through.
watching: Whether VIX 9-day, now above front-month VIX at 27.76, reverts to normal backwardation or keeps inverting.
Breakeven stabilization versus continued declines in 5-year and 10-year inflation compensation.
Follow-through in small caps and the Russell 2000 versus a fade back below Friday's close.
Dollar index behavior at fresh highs alongside a firmer gold price, a divergence that needs to resolve one way or the other.
note.equities:
Every major US index closed up, led by the Nasdaq 100 at +6.86% and the S&P 500 at +4.73%, with the Dow lagging at +3.01% on its lighter tech weight. The Russell 2000 at +3.40% and the S&P MidCap 400 at +3.42% moved in line with large caps, which is the detail that matters: this was not a mega-cap-only short squeeze, it reached the broad market.

Sector rotation was unambiguous. Technology led at +8.97%, Communications followed at +3.57%, and Consumer Discretionary added +3.98%, a trio of growth-sensitive groups moving together on the back of the chip and AI names. Energy was the one sector in the red at -1.06%, tracking the drop in crude, while Consumer Staples was flat at -0.09%. Breadth backed the move up: 20 advancers against 5 decliners, a ratio of 4.0, with dispersion at 6.64 showing the rally had real spread across names, not just the five megacaps in the leaders list.
note.rates:
The curve bear steepened, with 2s10s widening by 1bp to 29bp and 5s30s widening by 6bp to 60bp. Every tenor from 2-year to 30-year fell in yield, but the front end fell further: 2-year down 13bp to 4.63%, 5-year down 15bp to 4.71%, versus 30-year down only 9bp to 5.31%. The 3-month/10-year spread moved the other way, narrowing 10bp to 60bp.

Breakevens fell across the board and sit at session lows: the 5-year breakeven slipped 3bp to 2.15, the 10-year breakeven 2bp to 2.13, and the 5y5y forward 1bp to 2.11. The 10-year TIPS yield fell 11bp to 2.77%. A falling-yield, falling-breakeven combination with steepening at the back end is a market pricing lower growth risk premium at the front while term premium stays sticky further out. There is no auction detail in today's pack to add color on demand.
note.credit: Credit richened with equities. US high yield (HYG) rose +0.25% and the JNK high yield proxy rose +0.28%, both still sitting at YTD lows of roughly -5.14% and -5.59% respectively, so today's gain is a bounce inside a weak year, not a reversal of trend. Investment grade (LQD) added +0.23% and EM sovereign debt (EMB) outperformed at +0.87%, the single biggest mover in the credit complex and the strongest cross-asset confirmation of the risk-on tape. Leveraged loans (BKLN) were the outlier, down -0.05% on the day. Tone was constructive but the extremes list still flags US high yield at a session low, a reminder that spread compression has room before it signals real conviction.
note.fx: The dollar index rose +0.50% to 104.329, a fresh high alongside USD/CHF, USD/CAD, USD/MXN, USD/BRL and USD/TRY, a broad-based bid against both G10 and EM crosses. EUR/USD fell -0.58% to 1.091 and GBP/USD fell -0.41% to 1.303, both at session lows. USD/JPY was the exception, falling -0.45% to 158.985 even as the broader dollar index rose, a divergence worth flagging. In EM, USD/CNY eased -0.04% to 6.664 and USD/INR fell -0.42%, while USD/BRL softened -0.05% against the broader dollar strength, a mixed picture that does not read as a uniform EM selloff.
note.commodities: Energy sold off hard against the broader risk rally: WTI fell -4.44% to $80.25 and Brent fell -6.32% to $86.72, the two biggest moves of the session in either direction. Natural gas went the other way, up +3.69%. Precious metals rose alongside the stronger dollar, an unusual pairing: gold added +3.39% to $3,634.40 and silver jumped +4.76% to $42.99, both notable given DXY also printed a high. Copper rose +2.47% to $5.612, consistent with the broader risk bid, while aluminium fell -1.64%. Grains and softs were mostly firmer: wheat +3.53%, corn +3.34%, sugar +3.23%, cocoa +3.04%, with coffee the outlier at -2.73%.
note.volatility: The vol complex unwound sharply. VIX fell -25.83% to 26.62, VIX 3-month fell -17.58% to 25.50, and VVIX fell -14.97% to 117.36, all consistent with a rapid de-risking of hedges built up into the prior selloff. The one point of caution: VIX 9-day at 27.76 still sits above front-month VIX, an inversion that says the market is not yet fully confident the stress is behind it. SKEW ticked up +1.10% to 140.37, showing tail-risk pricing did not come in as fast as at-the-money vol did. Protection got cheaper today, but not uniformly across the curve.
note.digital: Digital assets did not participate in the equity rally. Bitcoin was roughly flat at -0.15% to $61,071.80, and Ether fell -0.77% to $1,707.80, both still showing steep YTD losses of -31.17% and -43.08% respectively. Solana and XRP bucked the group, up +1.90% and +0.77%. The lack of beta to today's equity rally in the two largest tokens suggests crypto is trading its own de-leveraging story rather than following the broader risk tape.
note.international: European markets closed broadly higher ahead of the US open, led by the EURO STOXX 50 at +2.23% and the DAX at +2.16%, with the FTSE 100 up +1.30%. Asia was weaker and mixed: the Hang Seng fell -0.12% to a session low, the KOSPI dropped -3.32%, and the Sensex fell -1.77%, while the TAIEX was the regional standout at +2.16%. The split handed New York a market already biased toward a US-specific bounce rather than a globally synchronized risk rally, consistent with the breakeven and dollar divergences seen through the session.
note.correlation:
The standout break today is the joint rally in equities and gold against a stronger dollar. Normally a firmer DXY (+0.50%) pressures gold; instead gold rose +3.39% alongside the dollar hitting session highs, while risk assets rallied hard. That combination looks more like a broad short-covering and deleveraging unwind across asset classes than a coordinated macro view, since a genuine growth-optimism rally would typically sell gold and bonds together, not buy both equities and precious metals.

The second break is in credit versus rates: spreads richened (HYG, EMB both up) even as the curve bear steepened, which is consistent with each other, but the breakeven decline alongside the bear-steepener in nominal yields is the one piece that does not fit. If breakevens keep falling while credit keeps buying risk, that divergence will eventually force one side to reprice. A durable rally needs breakevens to stop falling or credit to start pricing in the disinflation signal the TIPS market is sending.
